data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic root 'fadha' which means 'to give'. Fadwah signifies a precious gift or reward, often bestowed by Allah (SWT) or a loved one. The name Fadwah carries the meaning “Gift, Reward” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fadwah usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, reward and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine blessings and rewards, reflecting the grace and generosity of Allah (SWT).
data.etymology: Fadwah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift, Reward.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fadwah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Fadwah has strong cultural significance in the Arab world. Naming a child Fadwah is a beautiful sentiment, reflecting the values of giving, generosity, and gratitude that are deeply ingrained in Arab culture. The name evokes the idea of a reward or blessing bestowed upon a child, a divine or loving gift that sets them on their journey through life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name carries deep significance and meaning. Fadwah is often seen as a reminder of the blessings and gifts that come from Allah SWT and the importance of accepting and being grateful for them. It is also a powerful reminder of the importance of giving and helping others, as reflected in the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) words, "Give to the one who is unable to repay you." The name Fadwah inspires us to be givers, to seek and extend blessings, and to remember and appreciate the gifts that come our way.
